summary: Traivaix Pictures LLC is an independent film distributor based in New York. On March 2, 2026 it entered a Master Services Agreement with Zegath Post & Delivery, Inc., a Burbank post-production and delivery vendor. Under the MSA, Zegath creates digital cinema packages (DCPs), subtitles, dubbed audio tracks and festival screeners for Traivaix's release slate. The folder holds ten documents: the MSA, an amendment, a data processing addendum, Order Form No. 1, a volume-rebate side letter, the original term sheet, a content security and quality agreement, Zegath's notice of an intended assignment, kickoff meeting notes, and a certificate of insurance. Four problems are planted. (1) The side letter moves governing law and forum to California. (2) The quality agreement replaces the MSA section that the uncapped carve-out for content-security breaches points to. (3) The amendment lets Zegath assign freely, and Zegath has announced an assignment to a rival distributor. (4) The order form narrows the defined term 'Deliverables', which strips Traivaix of ownership of subtitle and dubbing files.

issues.label: governing law mismatch
issues.description: The MSA chooses New York law (Section 16.1) and the exclusive jurisdiction of New York County courts (Section 16.2). Section 4 of the side letter is dated August 3, 2026 and signed by both parties. It provides that the side letter, and any dispute arising out of or relating to the Agreement as modified by it, is governed by the laws of the State of California and resolved exclusively in the courts of Los Angeles County. MSA Section 2.3 ranks signed side letters above the MSA in the order of precedence, so the side letter's choice controls rather than being cured. The New York client is pushed into California law and a Los Angeles forum for all MSA disputes, or at least into a fight over which clause governs.
issues.expected_finding: Section 4 of the side letter applies California law and exclusive Los Angeles County jurisdiction to disputes under the Agreement as modified. Because MSA Section 2.3 gives signed side letters precedence over the MSA, this displaces the MSA's New York law and New York County forum. The side letter should be amended so that it defers expressly to MSA Sections 16.1 and 16.2.

issues.label: liability cap carve-out conflict
issues.description: MSA Section 11.3 caps each party's liability at fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months. Section 11.4(a) excludes from that cap any breach of Section 8 (Content Security), which covers pre-release leaks and screener piracy, the main catastrophic risk for a film distributor. On its own the MSA is favourable to Traivaix. The Quality Agreement, effective April 1, 2026, states in Section 1.2 that it replaces Section 8 of the MSA in its entirety with more detailed watermarking and screener-handling requirements. Section 9.1 of the Quality Agreement then makes Zegath's liability for breach of the Quality Agreement subject to the limitation in Section 11.3 of the MSA. Read alone, the Quality Agreement looks like an upgrade to security standards. MSA Section 2.3 ranks the Quality Agreement above the MSA. Read together, content-security breaches are no longer breaches of 'Section 8', so the Section 11.4(a) carve-out has nothing to attach to, and leak losses fall under the 12-month fee cap. Indemnities under Section 10 cover only third-party IP claims and do not reach leaks, so Section 11.4(b) does not rescue Traivaix.
issues.expected_finding: The Quality Agreement replaces MSA Section 8 and subjects its own breaches to the Section 11.3 cap, and it prevails under MSA Section 2.3. The MSA Section 11.4(a) carve-out for breaches of Section 8 therefore no longer reaches content-security failures, leaving pre-release leak losses capped at 12 months' fees. The carve-out should be amended to cover breaches of the Quality Agreement's content security requirements expressly.

issues.label: unrestricted assignment
issues.description: The term sheet records that neither party may assign without the other's prior written consent, and the original MSA Section 15.2 reflected that. Amendment No. 1, dated July 15, 2026, replaces MSA Section 15.2. Under the new clause Zegath may assign the Agreement and any Order Form, without the consent of Traivaix, to any Affiliate or to any successor to all or substantially all of its business or assets. Traivaix still needs Zegath's consent to assign. Under MSA Section 2.3 the amendment prevails. Zegath's notice letter dated October 6, 2026 states that its parent has signed a definitive agreement to be acquired by Ostrel Releasing Group, a competing independent distributor, and that Zegath will assign the MSA to Ostrel Media Services LLC on closing. A rival would then hold Traivaix's unreleased masters, release schedules and screener lists. The assignment has not yet occurred.
detect_terms: successor to all or substantially all
issues.expected_finding: Amendment No. 1 lets Zegath assign the MSA without Traivaix's consent to any successor, departing from the term sheet's mutual-consent restriction. Zegath's October 6, 2026 notice letter shows it intends to assign to an affiliate of competitor Ostrel Releasing Group on closing. Traivaix should promptly seek to restore its consent right or add a competitor-assignment prohibition with a termination right before the closing.

issues.label: defined term inconsistency
issues.description: MSA Section 1.1 defines 'Deliverables' broadly to include DCPs, subtitle files, dubbed audio and captions. Section 7.1 vests ownership of all Deliverables in Traivaix as work made for hire. Section 7.3 treats everything else as Zegath Materials, licensed to Traivaix non-exclusively only during the Term. Section 2.3 lets each Order Form control the description of the Services and Deliverables under it. Order Form No. 1, dated March 2, 2026, defines 'Deliverables' in Section 2 as the DCP masters for the Titles listed in Exhibit 1. Its Services, however, include subtitling into six languages and Spanish and French dubbing. Each clause looks ordinary alone. Together, the subtitle and dubbing files for the 2026 slate fall outside 'Deliverables' and become Zegath Materials. Traivaix loses ownership of them and its right to use them once the Term ends, which blocks later licensing windows.
issues.expected_finding: Order Form No. 1 defines Deliverables as DCP masters only, and that definition controls under MSA Section 2.3. The subtitle and dubbing files it orders therefore fall outside the MSA Section 7.1 work-made-for-hire ownership and become Zegath Materials licensed only during the Term. The Order Form should be amended to adopt the MSA definition of Deliverables or to list those localization materials expressly.
